title: Google Trends product-keyword attention vs Taiwan supply-chain weekly volatility

related_prior_experiments.K750: Real Google Trends fear index did not add robust volatility value beyond VIX; fear was reactive.
related_prior_experiments.K789: Return/tail-risk follow-up fell back to VIX-proxy and concluded no genuine Google Trends evidence.
related_prior_experiments.K1472: Rolling HAR framework template for honest low-frequency volatility proxy tests.

literature.citation: Da, Engelberg & Gao (2011), Journal of Finance
literature.note: Introduces Google Search Volume Index as a direct investor-attention proxy.

literature.citation: Vlastakis & Markellos (2012), Journal of Banking & Finance
literature.note: Studies Google Trends information demand and stock-market volatility.

literature.citation: Andrei & Hasler (2015), Review of Financial Studies
literature.note: Models investor attention and uncertainty as drivers of return variance.

literature.citation: Investor attention fluctuation and stock market volatility (2023), PLOS ONE
literature.note: Uses investor attention inside HAR-style volatility forecasting for China.

methodology.target: current-week close-to-close realized variance, sum of daily log-return squared
methodology.baseline: log-HAR weekly RV model with rv_lag1 / rv_lag4 / rv_lag13
methodology.candidate_increment: Google Trends composite attention lagged one week
methodology.lookahead_guard: attention_lag1 = attention.shift(1); no same-week search volume predicts same-week RV
methodology.evaluation: rolling expanding OOS, QLIKE, HAC DM-style loss-difference t-stat; Harvey |t|>3 gate

limitations: Google Trends is accessed through unofficial pytrends endpoints and may return HTTP 429.
Only real Google Trends terms that pass the minimum-week gate are used; no VIX/price proxy fills missing terms.
If Google only returns a partial historical panel, the conclusion is limited to that available panel.
Weekly Google Trends values are normalized by Google; stitched chunks are approximate even with overlap scaling.

predictive_results.attention_feature: mean rolling 52-week z-score across available Google Trends terms

conclusion: In the available real Google Trends panel, the lagged product-keyword composite did not robustly improve weekly RV forecasts versus HAR across the Taiwan supply-chain ticker family. This is a partial-panel NULL, not evidence that all product-search attention data are useless.

review.self_review: No replacement proxy is used when Google Trends is unavailable.
